 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.11,50,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 10092021 at about 12.15 p.m., when the Petitioner was playing in front of his house towards Byatarayanadoddi on the side of Shanubhoganahalli, at that time,
a two wheeler bearing No.KA51HN5910 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner.
Due to the tremondous impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Vijaya Shree Hospital,
wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient.

He has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/
towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was 7 years old student.

Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the motor cycle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel but not filed objection statement.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, it denied the age, education of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
It has contended that the owner of the motor cycle had entrusted the vehicle to the rider, who had no valid driving licence at the time of alleged accident.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.

sentences.text: 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 10.09.2021 at about 12.15 p.m. in front of the house of the Petitioner near Kanchagayanadoddi Village, Jigani, Anekal Taluk, Bangalore, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing No.KA51HN5910?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.15.
He also examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked 8 documents as per Ex.P16 to P23 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 9. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the minor Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 10092021 at about 12.15 p.m. due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Regn.No.KA51H5910.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.

11. In order to prove the case of the minor Petitioner, the guardian of the minor petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked 23 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P23.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, copy of policy, police information report, IMV report, copy of police notice, Wound Certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex . P.9
is the Medical bills, Ex. P.10 is the prescription, Ex. P.11 and 12 are the Xrays.
Ex. P.13 is is the advance bills.

Ex.
P.14 and 15 are Aadhar cards.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR and Ex.P2 Complaint shows that on the complaint lodged before Bannerghatta Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA51HN5910 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC r/w Sec.187 of MV Act.
Ex. P.3 is the policy.
Ex. P.4 is the police information report.

Ex. P.5 is the IMV report which shows that the accident was not due to any Thanmai Ram vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37135338/
3 mechanical defect of the motor vehicle.

sentences.text: Ex. P.6 is the notice under Section 133.
Ex . P.7
is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Ex . P7

is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Bannerghatta Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC r/w Sec.187 of MV Act.
Ex . P.9
is the medical bills.

is the advance bills.
Ex.P.14 and 15 are Aadhar cards.
13. Further, P.W.1 examined medical record officer by namely Dhanush K.N as PW.2 and Dr.Vivekananda B.R as P.W.3

and he also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
14.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
15. On the other hand, respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by both parties and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the PW.1 has proved the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA51HN5910 by its rider and in the said accident, the minor Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
16. Issue No. 2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. According to the Petitioner, he sustained fracture of tibia and fibula.
In this regard, next friend of the Petitioner, his father deposed as PW1 and relied on the Wound Certificate at Ex.P7.
As per the Wound Certificate, the Petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right tibia and fibula.
The said injury is grievous in nature.
The PW.1 deposed that his son was admitted as an inpatient from 10.09.2021 to 12.09.2021.
Further, P.W.3 Dr.Vivekananda.B.R has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
However, PW.1 has not produced any discharge summary.

18. The Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Vivekanand.B.R as PW3 and he deposed that he examined the minor Petitioner on 04102023 and found that the Petitioner is suffering from 16% Permanent disability to the right lower limb.
The age of the Petitioner is 6 years.
As such question of occupation and income does not arise.
In the circumstances, any disability shown to his limb cannot be assessed as functional disability.
19. According to the evidence of doctor/PW3, the minor Petitioner suffered physical disability at 16% to the right lower limb.
However, the doctor not assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner and no evidence is forthcoming in that regard.

In a decision passed in Civil Appeal No.7139/2013 (Master Mallikarjun Vs Division Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another)
by the Hon'ble Apex Court, it is held that if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole Thanmai Ram vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37135338/
4 body, the minor Petitioner would be entitled for compensation of Rs.3 lakhs in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendance etc., towards conventional heads like pain and sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship inconvenience,
discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.

sentences.text:
As noted above,
there is no assessment of whole body disability of the petitioner.

As such, having considered the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and its gravity it appears just and proper to this court to consider that the petitioner sustained whole body disability at the rate of 6%.
As such, the above quoted decision will not come to the aid of petitioner.
20. The medical records and the evidence produced in support of the same disclose the fact that petitioner sustained fracture of shaft of tibia and fibula.
Hence, there are certainly pain and sufferings.
As such, it appears just and proper to this court to award compensation of sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards pain and sufferings.

21. In addition to the compensation towards conventional heads, the minor Petitioner is also entitled for compensation under the heads like discomfort and inconvenience to the parents and their loss of earnings during the period of hospitalization of the Petitioner and towards medical expenditure.
With regard to the case on hand, the medical records disclosed that discharge summary is not produced.
However, the document Ex.P.13 discloses the fact that petitioner was admitted for two days at Vijayshree hospital from 10.9.2021 to 12.09.2021 and took treatment as an inpatient.
As such, it can be presumed that petitioner was inpatient for two days.
Upon consideration of the age of the petitioner, it is needless to mention that he might have been accompanied by his parents to the hospital during treatment.
As such, his parents might have lost their earnings during that period.
In the absence of proof of income of his parents, it would be lawful to award Rs.10,000/ as compensation towards loss of earnings and their discomfort.
22. With regard to medical expenditure, the PW.1 has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 14 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.9 which is totally amounting to Rs.9,72766/.
The PW.1 has produced advance bills at Ex. P.13 which are not included in these bills.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same are acceptable.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,800/as a compensation under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
23.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering, Rs. 1,00,000/ loss of amenities 2. Loss of income during Rs. 10,000/ the laid up period 3.

Medical expenditure Rs. 9,800/ Total Rs.1,19,800/
24.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.1,19,800/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA51 HN5910.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.1,19,800/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1,
Rs.10,000/ shall be released in favour of the father of the minor petitioner as medical expenses borne by him by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of minor in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank until he attains the age of majority.
The guardian/father of the minor Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
